judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital is a mechanical list of principal amounts (which do sum to the $147,485,000 on the cover) but it creates two labels — 'Series 2004 Bonds' and 'Series 2004 Auction Bonds' — for the same instruments with the loose phrase 'being sometimes referred to together herein', leaving unclear when each label controls. judgments.reasoning_cat1: A factual recital of appointment and of the Company's direction under Section 2.6(a) of the Auction Agreement; the only wobble is the OCR 'bas been appointed'. Nothing in the words admits two readings.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single clause stating that the Auction Procedures require one or more Broker-Dealers; it is definite and purely introductory. Nothing to name as ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.1(c) (c011), which contemplates other Persons executing Broker-Dealer Agreements. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deeming rule turns 'purchase', 'sale' and 'holding' into beneficial ownership interests 'unless the context clearly requires otherwise', a self-referential escape hatch whose boundary a court would have to draw. judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 2.5(b)'s (c025) rules about who remains the Broker-Dealer on transfers and with 2.6(a)'s (c027) delivery mechanics, both of which assume beneficial-interest trading; no contradiction surfaced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any reference herein to Bonds or Auction Bonds shall be deemed to be references to each series of Series 2004 Bonds and Series 2004 Auction Bonds' collapses two defined terms that the recital already treats as coextensive, so its operative effect is uncertain. The second sentence's 'apply separately to each series' pulls the other way from the first sentence's aggregation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against recital c001, which says the Series 2004 Bonds are 'sometimes' called the Series 2004 Auction Bonds, this deeming clause leaves genuinely unclear whether a series-specific obligation (e.g. the fee formula in 2.5(b)) is computed per series or in aggregate. judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard due-authorisation and enforceability warranty with the usual 'assuming the due authorization, execution and delivery' qualifier; every term is a term of art. Nothing here carries two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It assumes due execution only 'by the Auction Agent' although the Company is also a signatory party to this three-party agreement, a small gap rather than a conflict; nothing in Sections 2-5 contradicts the warranty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision defines 'Auction' by reference to each periodic implementation of the Auction Procedures and is definite except that 'Initial Periods' is not defined here. The sentence structure is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the Auction Procedures incorporated by 2.1(b) (c010) and matches recital c003's description of the Auction Rate; no inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A blanket incorporation of 'all of the provisions' of the Auction Procedures and Settlement Procedures 'in their entirety' without identifying the document or edition from which they come — the reach of the incorporation is exactly the kind of thing courts construe. judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls in an unbounded body of external terms while 5.4 (c035) declares this agreement plus the issuance documents to be the entire agreement and 3.1(b) (c030) limits the Auction Agent to duties 'expressly set forth herein, or expressly incorporated herein by reference pursuant to Section 2.1(b)'. judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'BD agrees to handle customer orders in accordance with its respective duties under applicable securities laws and rules' imports an undefined external standard into a contractual promise, and 'the obligations of, and limitations and restrictions placed upon, a Broker-Dealer' is stated without saying where those obligations are found. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 2.3(b) (c017), which frames BD's role as implementing Auctions to achieve 'the lowest possible interest rate', an unrestricted right to bid for its own account is in tension with that stated purpose, and 5.5 (c036) would deny the Company a remedy even though this clause gives the Company the prohibition power. judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed deadline and two named items to be communicated; 'other electronic communication acceptable to the parties' is the only soft phrase and it is a common formulation. Little to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with 2.2(b)'s (c014) disclosure carve-out keyed to indemnity satisfactory to the Auction Agent and with 3.1(b)'s express-duties-only rule. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel disclaimers exist for the Auction Agent in 3.1(a)-(b) (c029, c030) but none for BD, which sharpens the argument that implied obligations of good faith attach to BD's undertakings in 2.3(b) (c017) and 2.1(d) (c012).
